title: `slog`: structured logging in the standard library

videos.script: A log written as sentences is easy to read and hard to search. This lesson writes records instead. {{record}} A record has a level, a message and named values. A handler turns it into bytes: text for a person at a terminal, or one JSON object per line for a machine. {{attrs}} Then attributes. A logger made with With adds a request id to every line, once. A group nests values. And a token type that knows how to log itself never leaks into a log by accident. {{badkey}} One argument short, and the record says so out loud. go vet catches it first. {{levels}} Last, the two things an incident asks for. A level you can lower while the program runs. And a handler that takes the request id from the context, so code deep in the call never needs to know about it. {{close}} Lesson 23 is about regular expressions, and what one can cost.
